name: Advanced Seminar Innovation & Entrepreneurship: Entrepreneurial Role Models
description:
The course exposes students to the people side of entrepreneurship. Students will learn to understand and explain entrepreneurial behavior through the stories of role models of their preference, from fiction (books, novels, movies, etc.) as well as entrepreneurs from both historical and contemporary contexts. They analyze these role models based on models and theories from entrepreneurship research.

At a more abstract level, this course prepares students for their Master's Thesis by fostering and deepening their understanding of (1) searching, understanding, and analyzing the academic literature, (2) the systematic analysis of an empirical example, and (3) the effective writing of academic papers. Moreover, students learn to give presentations to an academic audience and how to discuss research insights.
prerequisites: Good English language skills are required.
